title: Privacy Policy
description: How Acru collects, uses, discloses, retains, and protects personal information across our services.

introduction.text: Acru, Inc. (“Acru,” “we,” “us,” or “our”) respects your privacy and is committed to protecting Personal Information entrusted to us.

This Privacy Policy explains how Acru collects, uses, discloses, retains, and protects Personal Information when you interact with our website, applications, payment technologies, dashboards, portals, APIs, merchant onboarding services, affiliate and referral programs, customer support channels, and other products and services that link to this Privacy Policy (collectively, the “Services”).
This Privacy Policy applies to, among others:

items: Business owners, officers, directors, employees, beneficial owners, and authorized representatives of merchants;
Affiliates, referral partners, agents, and other business partners;
Users of Acru dashboards, portals, APIs, or other technology;
Customers or end users who transact with merchants using payment functionality facilitated through Acru or our partners;
Individuals who communicate with Acru or request support; and
Other individuals whose Personal Information we process in connection with providing the Services.

introduction.text: “Personal Information” or “Personal Data” means information that identifies, relates to, describes, is reasonably capable of being associated with, or could reasonably be linked to an individual or household. The definition does not include information excluded from applicable privacy laws, such as certain publicly available, aggregated, or deidentified information.

sections.heading: 1. Acru’s Role in the Payment Ecosystem

blocks.text: Acru provides technology and services designed to help merchants access and manage payment-processing capabilities.

Depending on the product, jurisdiction, transaction, and commercial relationship involved, certain payment-processing, acquiring, banking, card-network, identity-verification, underwriting, compliance, settlement, fraud-prevention, chargeback, or other financial functions may be performed by third-party processors, acquiring banks, financial institutions, payment networks, technology providers, or other partners.

Acru may provide the merchant-facing interface through which information is submitted to these partners. For example, information submitted through an Acru merchant application may be transmitted to one or more payment-processing or financial partners for:

items: Know Your Customer (“KYC”) or identity verification;
Anti-money laundering or sanctions screening where applicable;
Compliance with applicable laws, payment-network rules, or financial-institution requirements.

blocks.text: Those organizations may process Personal Information under their own privacy policies and legal obligations. Acru does not control the independent privacy practices of banks, card networks, payment processors, or other financial institutions when they process information independently from Acru.

sections.heading: 2. When Acru Acts for a Merchant

blocks.text: In certain circumstances, Acru may process Personal Information on behalf of a merchant or other business customer. For example, a merchant may transmit information about its customers to Acru through an integration, API, dashboard, payment flow, or other Service.

When Acru processes Personal Information solely on behalf of a merchant, the merchant may be the “controller” or “business,” and Acru may be a “processor” or “service provider,” as those terms are defined by applicable privacy laws.
If you are a customer of an Acru merchant and have questions about how that merchant uses your Personal Information, you should review the merchant’s privacy policy and contact the merchant directly.
Where required or appropriate, Acru will assist merchants in responding to privacy requests concerning Personal Information that Acru processes on their behalf.

Acru may separately act as a controller or business with respect to information that Acru uses for its own legitimate purposes, including fraud prevention, security, legal compliance, platform administration, billing, merchant risk management, and protection of Acru and its partners.

blocks.text: Automated systems may consider information such as transaction history, merchant activity, device information, fraud signals, account information, chargeback patterns, processing behavior, identity-verification results, and information supplied by financial or fraud-prevention partners.

In some cases, a bank, processor, card network, or other independent partner may make its own decision concerning merchant approval, transaction authorization, account restrictions, settlement, or other financial matters.
Where applicable law grants rights concerning qualifying automated decision-making or profiling, you may exercise those rights as described in the Your Privacy Rights section below.

sections.heading: 10. Global Privacy Control and Do Not Track

blocks.text: Some browsers allow users to transmit privacy preference signals.

Where required by applicable law, Acru recognizes qualifying opt-out preference signals, including Global Privacy Control (“GPC”), as requests to opt out of certain sale, sharing, or targeted-advertising activities.

Because there is not currently a universally accepted legal or technical standard for all “Do Not Track” signals, Acru may not respond to traditional Do Not Track settings unless required by applicable law.

sections.heading: 16. How to Exercise Your Privacy Rights

blocks.text: To submit a privacy request, contact Acru at legal@acru.com. Please state the type of request you wish to make and provide sufficient information for us to identify the relevant records.

We may need to verify your identity before completing certain requests. Verification may require us to confirm information reasonably associated with your account or relationship with Acru. We will not request additional information beyond what is reasonably necessary to authenticate the request.
Where permitted by law, you may use an authorized agent to submit a request. We may require evidence that the agent is authorized to act on your behalf and may separately verify your identity.
If Acru denies a privacy request and applicable law provides an appeal right, instructions for appealing the decision will be included in our response.
